summary: myseliasan's control plane was a passive relay that only showed a node's status when someone opened the Nodes page; it now proactively alerts on fleet health. The heartbeat reconciler (services/node_registry.go) edge-triggers a notification in the unified feed the instant a node goes online→lost (once, not repeated while it stays lost), when a lost node recovers, and when a node's certificate is within its renewal warn window of expiring or has already expired (deduped per distinct expiry, so a renewal re-arms the warning). The warn window defaults to 7 days and is wired from the existing pairing.renewBeforeHours config (previously only consulted by the node side for its own renewal, so this makes a config key that already existed do double duty rather than adding a new one). A new GET /api/nodes/fleet-status endpoint returns a fleet-wide rollup (total/online/lost/selfDropped/unknown/certsExpiring/certsExpired/certWarnDays), and the Dashboard gained a 'Certs expiring' KPI card fed by it. Separately, ingestNodeEvent no longer silently drops node-pushed event kinds it doesn't recognize (health/disk-full/alert/system/etc.) — it now surfaces them in the notification feed with a best-effort category/severity guess instead of discarding them.
compatibility: Backward compatible for existing installs: no schema change (reuses the existing ManagedNode/CertExpiresAt fields and the shared notification store), no new config keys required. Existing pairing.renewBeforeHours values (or its 48h default) now also drive the control-plane cert-expiry warning; installs relying on that key's prior node-side-only renewal behavior are unaffected. Fleet-health notifications land in the existing unified feed (category health.check, source node:<id>) alongside node-pushed events, so no new notification-delivery config is needed for them to reach existing webhook/telegram/MQTT destinations subscribed to that category.
